TEXT.English: The Proprietor's abilities are limited to cities where the Council of Esus religion has already spread. As long as you have enough gold to spend, they can steal Culture or Great Person Points and transfer them to your capital. Alternatively, you can use their [BOLD]Forgery[\BOLD] ability to boost the Culture of your city based on its current Crime.

TEXT.English: The Death Merchant's abilities are limited to cities where the Council of Esus religion has already spread. If you have enough gold, a Death Merchant can set up an [BOLD]Arms Smuggling Operation[\BOLD] in one of your cities to boost military production at the cost of increasing the local crimerate.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Alternatively, Death Merchants can be used to economically sabotage your opponent's cities by increasing their Crime, or as a means of quickly gaining gold in your own cities through their [BOLD]Illicit Trade[\BOLD] ability.

TEXT.English: Whispers are alternatives to assassins available to civilizations that adopt the Council of Esus as their state religion. While their base strength is weaker than a normal assassin, they make up for it with a higher level of Invisibility and the ability to cast Shadow I (which can be used to support a stack of units) and Shadow II spells (which can be used to buff themselves or a stack).

TEXT.English: Enforcers serve as cheap units available to civilizations that have converted to the Council of Esus.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]While initially weaker than other units in their tier, so long as they are near a city you control, their strength will scale based on its Crime. Any unit they promote to will retain this ability.
